1. // Copyright The OpenTelemetry Authors
2. // SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
3. 
4. // Package componentstatus is an experimental module that defines how components should
5. // report health statues, how collector hosts should facilitate component status reporting,
6. // and how extensions should watch for new component statuses.
7. //
8. // This package is currently under development and is exempt from the Collector SIG's
9. // breaking change policy.
10. package componentstatus // import "go.opentelemetry.io/collector/component/componentstatus"
11. 
12. import (
13. 	"time"
14. 
15. 	"go.opentelemetry.io/collector/component"
16. )
17. 
18. // Reporter is an extra interface for `component.Host` implementations.
19. // A Reporter defines how to report a `componentstatus.Event`.
20. type Reporter interface {
21. 	// Report allows a component to report runtime changes in status. The service
22. 	// will automatically report status for a component during startup and shutdown. Components can
23. 	// use this method to report status after start and before shutdown. For more details about
24. 	// component status reporting see: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/docs/component-status.md
25. 	Report(*Event)
26. }
27. 
28. // Watcher is an extra interface for Extension hosted by the OpenTelemetry
29. // Collector that is to be implemented by extensions interested in changes to component
30. // status.
31. //
32. // TODO: consider moving this interface to a new package/module like `extension/statuswatcher`
33. // https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/10764
34. type Watcher interface {
35. 	// ComponentStatusChanged notifies about a change in the source component status.
36. 	// Extensions that implement this interface must be ready that the ComponentStatusChanged
37. 	// may be called before, after or concurrently with calls to Component.Start() and Component.Shutdown().
38. 	// The function may be called concurrently with itself.
39. 	ComponentStatusChanged(source *InstanceID, event *Event)
40. }
41. 
42. type Status int32
43. 
44. // Enumeration of possible component statuses
45. const (
46. 	// StatusNone indicates absence of component status.
47. 	StatusNone Status = iota
48. 	// StatusStarting indicates the component is starting.
49. 	StatusStarting
50. 	// StatusOK indicates the component is running without issues.
51. 	StatusOK
52. 	// StatusRecoverableError indicates that the component has experienced a transient error and may recover.
53. 	StatusRecoverableError
54. 	// StatusPermanentError indicates that the component has detected a condition at runtime that will need human intervention to fix. The collector will continue to run in a degraded mode.
55. 	StatusPermanentError
56. 	// StatusFatalError indicates that the collector has experienced a fatal runtime error and will shut down.
57. 	StatusFatalError
58. 	// StatusStopping indicates that the component is in the process of shutting down.
59. 	StatusStopping
60. 	// StatusStopped indicates that the component has completed shutdown.
61. 	StatusStopped
62. )
63. 
64. // String returns a string representation of a Status
65. func (s Status) String() string {
66. 	switch s {
67. 	case StatusStarting:
68. 		return "StatusStarting"
69. 	case StatusOK:
70. 		return "StatusOK"
71. 	case StatusRecoverableError:
72. 		return "StatusRecoverableError"
73. 	case StatusPermanentError:
74. 		return "StatusPermanentError"
75. 	case StatusFatalError:
76. 		return "StatusFatalError"
77. 	case StatusStopping:
78. 		return "StatusStopping"
79. 	case StatusStopped:
80. 		return "StatusStopped"
81. 	}
82. 	return "StatusNone"
83. }
84. 
85. // Event contains a status and timestamp, and can contain an error
86. type Event struct {
87. 	status Status
88. 	err    error
89. 	// TODO: consider if a timestamp is necessary in the default Event struct or is needed only for the healthcheckv2 extension
90. 	// https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/10763
91. 	timestamp time.Time
92. }
93. 
94. // Status returns the Status (enum) associated with the Event
95. func (ev *Event) Status() Status {
96. 	return ev.status
97. }
98. 
99. // Err returns the error associated with the Event.
100. func (ev *Event) Err() error {
101. 	return ev.err
102. }
103. 
104. // Timestamp returns the timestamp associated with the Event
105. func (ev *Event) Timestamp() time.Time {
106. 	return ev.timestamp
107. }
108. 
109. // NewEvent creates and returns a Event with the specified status and sets the timestamp
110. // time.Now(). To set an error on the event for an error status use one of the dedicated
111. // constructors (e.g. NewRecoverableErrorEvent, NewPermanentErrorEvent, NewFatalErrorEvent)
112. func NewEvent(status Status) *Event {
113. 	return &Event{
114. 		status:    status,
115. 		timestamp: time.Now(),
116. 	}
117. }
118. 
119. // NewRecoverableErrorEvent wraps a transient error
120. // passed as argument as a Event with a status StatusRecoverableError
121. // and a timestamp set to time.Now().
122. func NewRecoverableErrorEvent(err error) *Event {
123. 	ev := NewEvent(StatusRecoverableError)
124. 	ev.err = err
125. 	return ev
126. }
127. 
128. // NewPermanentErrorEvent wraps an error requiring human intervention to fix
129. // passed as argument as a Event with a status StatusPermanentError
130. // and a timestamp set to time.Now().
131. func NewPermanentErrorEvent(err error) *Event {
132. 	ev := NewEvent(StatusPermanentError)
133. 	ev.err = err
134. 	return ev
135. }
136. 
137. // NewFatalErrorEvent wraps the fatal runtime error passed as argument as a Event
138. // with a status StatusFatalError and a timestamp set to time.Now().
139. func NewFatalErrorEvent(err error) *Event {
140. 	ev := NewEvent(StatusFatalError)
141. 	ev.err = err
142. 	return ev
143. }
144. 
145. // StatusIsError returns true for error statuses (e.g. StatusRecoverableError,
146. // StatusPermanentError, or StatusFatalError)
147. func StatusIsError(status Status) bool {
148. 	return status == StatusRecoverableError ||
149. 		status == StatusPermanentError ||
150. 		status == StatusFatalError
151. }
152. 
153. // ReportStatus is a helper function that handles checking if the component.Host has implemented Reporter.
154. // If it has, the Event is reported. Otherwise, nothing happens.
155. func ReportStatus(host component.Host, e *Event) {
156. 	statusReporter, ok := host.(Reporter)
157. 	if ok {
158. 		statusReporter.Report(e)
159. 	}
160. }
161.

43. func newCommand(params otelcol.CollectorSettings) *cobra.Command {

10. )
11. 
12. const (
13. 	stability = component.StabilityLevelDevelopment
14. )
15. 
16. // NewFactory creates a new TUI exporter factory.
17. func NewFactory() exporter.Factory {
18. 	return exporter.NewFactory(
19. 		component.MustNewType("tui"),
20. 		createDefaultConfig,
21. 		exporter.WithTraces(createTraces, stability),
22. 		exporter.WithMetrics(createMetrics, stability),
23. 		exporter.WithLogs(createLogs, stability),
24. 	)
25. }
26. 
27. func createDefaultConfig() component.Config {
28. 	return &Config{}
29. }
30. 
31. func createTraces(ctx context.Context, set exporter.Settings, cfg component.Config) (exporter.Traces, error) {
32. 	oCfg := cfg.(*Config)
33. 
34. 	e, err := exporters.LoadOrStore(
35. 		oCfg,
36. 		func() (*tuiExporter, error) {
37. 			return newTuiExporter(oCfg), nil
38. 		},
39. 		&set.TelemetrySettings,
40. 	)
41. 	if err != nil {
42. 		return nil, err
43. 	}
44. 
45. 	return exporterhelper.NewTracesExporter(ctx, set, oCfg,
46. 		e.Unwrap().pushTraces,
47. 		exporterhelper.WithStart(e.Start),
48. 		exporterhelper.WithShutdown(e.Shutdown),
49. 	)
50. }
51. 
52. func createMetrics(ctx context.Context, set exporter.Settings, cfg component.Config) (exporter.Metrics, error) {
53. 	oCfg := cfg.(*Config)
54. 
55. 	e, err := exporters.LoadOrStore(
56. 		oCfg,
57. 		func() (*tuiExporter, error) {
58. 			return newTuiExporter(oCfg), nil
59. 		},
60. 		&set.TelemetrySettings,
61. 	)
62. 	if err != nil {
63. 		return nil, err
64. 	}
65. 
66. 	return exporterhelper.NewMetricsExporter(ctx, set, oCfg,
67. 		e.Unwrap().pushMetrics,
68. 		exporterhelper.WithStart(e.Start),
69. 		exporterhelper.WithShutdown(e.Shutdown),
70. 	)
71. }
72. 
73. func createLogs(ctx context.Context, set exporter.Settings, cfg component.Config) (exporter.Logs, error) {
74. 	oCfg := cfg.(*Config)
75. 
76. 	e, err := exporters.LoadOrStore(
77. 		oCfg,
78. 		func() (*tuiExporter, error) {
79. 			return newTuiExporter(oCfg), nil
80. 		},
81. 		&set.TelemetrySettings,
82. 	)
83. 	if err != nil {
84. 		return nil, err
85. 	}
86. 
87. 	return exporterhelper.NewLogsExporter(ctx, set, oCfg,
88. 		e.Unwrap().pushLogs,
89. 		exporterhelper.WithStart(e.Start),
90. 		exporterhelper.WithShutdown(e.Shutdown),
91. 	)
92. }
93. 
94. // This is the map of already created OTLP receivers for particular configurations.
95. // We maintain this map because the Factory is asked trace and metric receivers separately
96. // when it gets CreateTracesReceiver() and CreateMetricsReceiver() but they must not
97. // create separate objects, they must use one otlpReceiver object per configuration.
98. // When the receiver is shutdown it should be removed from this map so the same configuration
99. // can be recreated successfully.
100. var exporters = sharedcomponent.NewMap[*Config, *tuiExporter]()
